findings.reason: a node implementing §15 as written reaches a case its gate requires to proceed and that the mechanism refuses, so it either blocks on (b1) or invents the missing canonical-exit read, and the plan must name that read (the canonical exit receipt, or a widened `_retired_attempt_ended` that also answers the canonical shape) before dispatch.
findings.text: §15 frees an off-host refusal on "the canonical `exit.json` beside a canonical `worker.json`", but the only two changes it declares are routing a foreign unknown reading into the placed-unknown branch and giving `_retired_attempt_ended` the launching-host rule; neither reads a canonical exit receipt, and `_retired_attempt_ended` is skipped entirely while `worker.json` exists, so the branch's last word is `_worker_record_liveness(record) is not False`, which answers `None` for a foreign record whatever `exit.json` says. Probe (scratch copy, `RECKON_HOME` redirected): with a foreign record carrying `worker.json` + `exit.json`, `live_worker_reading` returns `unknown/None`, `_worker_record_liveness` returns `None`, and the described mechanism returns `True` (refused) — done-when (b1) cannot pass

findings.reason: (2)'s repair targets a directory that is already there, and its required "fresh-launch marker" case would pass at the dispatch base, so the node would either chase a non-defect or contrive an empty-brief launch to make its own control fail; the real defect is the fresh launch reading its own marker as a relaunch, which is (1)'s mechanism and is what a single corrected statement of the cause should carry.
findings.text: §16's item (1) has the shadow arm's first launch "finds `attempt.json`" and take a reservation, while item (2) says the early marker at `dispatch.py:2772` "is dropped for an ordinary fresh launch" because the run directory "is created only later (near line 2894)"; both cannot hold, and the code sides with (1): `_store_brief` writes the brief into the run directory at `dispatch.py:2558` and `runs.store_brief` creates that directory (`destination.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)`, `reckon/crew/runs.py:703`) whenever the node carries a brief, so the marker at 2772 lands for an ordinary fresh launch. This run's own directory is the evidence: `r-20261109T133759173326-…` is a fresh run id, `brief.md` was written at 14:38:52 and `attempt-1.reservation` exists at 14:39:53, which is only possible if `run_holds_an_attempt_record` saw an `attempt.json` at `dispatch.py:2861` — the marker (2) says is dropped
